text:
maya: heads-up — ap-southeast GPU thin-pool (gpu-thin-pool-3) started evicting inference pods ~10:12 UTC. telemetry shows 5xx spike and queue growth on region-router. customers seeing timeouts.
ops-bot: alert created (INC-4882) — node-eviction-rate > 30% over 5m, autoscaler activity increased.
liam: on it, pulling node events and kubelet logs. any recent kernel/kernel-params changes?
maya: not on this cluster. we rolled a kernel patch to a different AZ yesterday but not here.
jorge: seeing repeated OOMKILL entries and /dev/nvme IO spikes on a subset of nodes. NVMe GC?
kate: can you post the dashboard link?
liam: dashboard -> https://grafana.redwood/ci/d/regions/ap-southeast?panel=pod-evictions (paste) :eyes:
liam: immediate plan: 1) stop scheduling to affected thin pool 2) shift traffic to reserve-pool-1 in same region (cold reserve) 3) if reserve saturation > 70% then do cross-region shift to ap-east with weight 60/40 fallback.
maya: agree. can we avoid full cross-region shift to reduce egress/cost? prefer cold reserve in-region first.
jorge: cold reserve is at 58% used now, we should be able to absorb short term. starting soft drain on nodes in thin-pool-3 to free up cache without evicting live sessions: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-aps-3a-0 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 node/gpu-aps-3a-0`
liam: note: current runbook drain step uses --grace-period=300. suggest we add a fast-drain variant for cache-sensitive pods. will open runbook PR.
kate: I'm going to flip routing to reserve-pool-1 via routing API now: `POST /v1/routing/shift` payload `{ \"from\":\"gpu-thin-pool-3\",\"to\":\"reserve-pool-1\",\"weight\":100 }`
ops-bot: routing change applied (shift-id rshift-992).
maya: telemetry shows queue length flattening, errors dropping but latency slightly higher : 200ms -> 280ms. still under SLO.
liam: action items emerging: 1) add eviction threshold alert to runbook (current only monitors node CPU/mem), 2) add fast-drain CLI snippet, 3) document NVMe healthcheck and auto-temp-throttle, 4) pre-emptive reserve warmup plan for peak windows.
jorge: also recommend a safety for our autoscaler that prevents simultaneous full-decommit of reserve pools when thin pools self-evict; it caused oscillation in this event.
kate: I can own a runbook PR to add these. will include exact CLI snippets, telemetry queries, and cost notes for cross-region shift.
maya: cost question — what is expected delta if we need to do sustained cross-region shift for 2 hours?
liam: estimate: egress + burst instances ~ $1.6k/hour for our avg load on ap-southeast -> ap-east. Cold reserve in-region is cheaper (~$0.45k/hour headroom). we'll prefer that unless reserve > 70%.
maya: good. put the cost thresholds in the runbook so on-call can make tradeoffs quickly.
liam: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/pull/209 — adds eviction checks, `fast-drain` snippet, and autoscaler protection.
sre-runbooks: reviewing PR now. a couple of comments: add a playbook step to verify KV cache warmup after shift (queries to cache-hit-rate panel) and include rollback command for routing shift id.
jorge: added NVMe SMART quick-check command to PR notes: `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1 | grep temperature` and `iostat -x 1 3 | grep nvme`
kate: updated the runbook to include a short decision matrix: if reserve < 65% -> in-region shift; 65-80% -> staged shift 80/20; >80% -> full cross-region with approved cost override. also added the cost estimates.
maya: excellent. can we also add a small unit test to CI that validates the routing API rollback path?
liam: yes, adding `test-routing-rollback` to runbook CI. will mock a shift and assert `rollback` returns 200 and routes revert.
ops-bot: incident INC-4882 marked RESOLVED by maya at 11:17 UTC. final notes: thin-pool-3 NVMe SMART showed elevated temperature + firmware GC bug. hardware ticket created (HW-1139).
maya: closing loop — runbook PR merged and deployed. follow-up items: 1) firmware upgrade schedule for affected node class, 2) add automated NVMe thermal alert, 3) review reserve warmup schedule for APAC peaks. assigning to infra-sched next sprint.
kate: thumbs-up :thumbsup:
liam: adding retrospective note to incident channel with timelines and cost analysis.
jorge: small ask — add a postmortem checklist item to verify no parallel reserved pool decommits during recovery.
sre-runbooks: added to playbook as hard step.
maya: thanks team. good catch on NVMe. we'll track HW-1139 and the runbook follow-ups.
